 FORT MYERS, Fla. (WINK) — The Rays and Brewers are each playing for their first World Series title, and one Milwaukee coach has roots in Southwest Florida.
 Daniel Vogelbach is a Bishop Verot grad and former major leaguer. WINK News reporter Lauren Halpern spoke with his older brother about the family connection behind this World Series trip.
 The Vogelbach brothers are seven years apart, but they were both standout athletes at Bishop Verot. Josh once held Lee County's career passing yards record.
 “Growing up, he was always super competitive. He wanted to fit in, hang out with the older guys, the big boys. So, I think that helped him throughout his life, he was kind of always just kind of fighting to survive.” Josh Vogelbach, offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Bishop Verot, said.
 Long before the big leagues, Daniel Vogelbach was the little brother trying to keep up. Josh runs Bishop Verot's offense, and even with a World Series ahead, Daniel is checking in.
 "He texts me this morning asking me or telling me good luck and asking me how I thought the game was going to go," Vogelbach said. "I was like, bro, you're about to coach in the World Series, like we'll be here when you get back, like, but that's a bond we have."
 After nine seasons as a major league player, Daniel is in his first year as Brewers hitting coach. It's his second year coaching in the big leagues.
 "Daniel was a great player, but I truly believe that he was born to be a coach," Vogelbach said. "He connects with people, connects with kids, now adults, and he has a special talent for that, and I'm just happy for him."
 Different sports, different teams, but Vogelbach said both brothers still lean on the lessons they learned at Bishop Verot.
 "The things that you're taught here at Verot in character, accountability, responsibility, that just helps you be successful in life," Vogelbach said.
 Vogelbach plans to catch the games in Tampa. If the series goes the distance, he may miss a Friday night at Bishop Verot to watch in Milwaukee.
